question.html:
a

A pure radioactive sample of bismuth-204 20483Bi is placed near a detector, which is connected to a counter.



Bismuth-204 decays into lead 20482Pb by beta-plus decay according to the equation 20483Bi→20482Pb+e++ν. The graph shows the variation with time t of the count rate R.


a.i State the background count rate. [1]

a.ii Estimate the half-life of 20483Bi. [3]

a.iii State and explain how the binding energy per nucleon of 20482Pb compares with that of 20483Bi. [2]

a.iv The distance between the sample and the detector is 20 cm. State why this would be an inappropriate distance for a sample that decayed by alpha decay. [1]

b

The following data are available for nuclear masses:

bismuth = 203.932254 u

lead = 203.928034 u

Calculate the energy released in the decay of one nucleus of bismuth-204.

[2]
